title: Gilgamesh: Kingship and Excess
subtitle: Greatness begins as a social problem

learningObjectives.text: Identify the main source-grounded idea in Gilgamesh: Kingship and Excess.
Distinguish primary, collection, synthesis, folklore, and reception evidence.

ref-primary.locator: Primary scaffold source — Gilgamesh: Kingship and Excess
ref-primary.excerpt: An edited translation of Old Babylonian tablets; fragmentary evidence requires careful citation.
ref-primary.note: Use the named collection/translation and preserve its dated or editorial frame.

ref-secondary.note: Use as a second source lens; do not blend separate traditions into one canon.

narrativeBlocks.title: Gilgamesh: Kingship and Excess
narrativeBlocks.body: Gilgamesh’s power is magnificent and destructive before friendship and loss reshape him.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the first source adds
narrativeBlocks.body: The first corpus source gives the broad story-world and vocabulary. Keep its editor, translator, and date in view rather than treating it as a neutral myth file.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the second source adds
narrativeBlocks.body: The second corpus record gives a different genre, region, or editorial lens. Comparing them helps you see where a tradition is stable and where it varies.

narrativeBlocks.title: How to read this tradition
narrativeBlocks.body: Ask who preserved the story, what kind of work it appears in, whether it is primary myth, folklore, synthesis, or reception, and what claim the passage can actually support.

narrativeBlocks.title: The cross-pantheon hook
narrativeBlocks.body: This gives you a comparative theme, not a blended canon. Keep the source boundary attached while you connect it to other pantheons.
